Gel Pedicure vs. Regular Polish: Which Should You Choose?

Choose gel or regular toenail polish by weighing curing, removal, finish, wear, budget, footwear, and the timing of your next color change.

By Element Nail Bar Editorial TeamSeptember 5, 2026Updated September 22, 20265 min read

In this guide

gel pedicure vs regular pedicureCompare services →View menu & pricing →

Answer

Choose Gel Polish when you want the separately listed lamp-cured finish. Choose regular polish when you want the finish already included with the selected base pedicure. Wear and removal can vary, so ask the salon about those details instead of treating the finish name as a durability or safety promise.

That distinction prevents a common booking mistake. Selecting gel does not identify a base pedicure. First choose one of the eight current base pedicures by its exact booking name, price, and total duration. Then add Gel Polish if that is the finish you want.

Gel and regular polish side by side

Decision pointGel polishRegular polish
Setting the finishCured under the salon’s compatible lampAir-dries over time
Leaving the appointmentFinish is set after curingNeeds protection from shoes and pressure while it finishes drying
WearVaries with the guest, finish, and aftercare; no duration is promised hereVaries with the guest, finish, and aftercare; no duration is promised here
RemovalAsk the salon which removal booking applies to the product already presentAsk the salon which removal booking applies to the product already present
Cost at Element 16Pedicure Gel Polish add-on is currently $15Included as the standard finish with listed pedicure tiers
Best forTrips, events, closed shoes soon after service, or fewer color changesFlexible color changes, simple removal, and budget-conscious maintenance

The active Element 16 booking contract lists Gel Polish for pedicures at exactly $15 for 15 minutes. Other selected services or add-ons remain separate booking items and are not implied by that Gel Polish price.

Start with your next two weeks, not a durability slogan

Marketing language can make gel sound like the automatic winner. It is not. A finish is useful when it fits what happens after the appointment.

Gel Polish is a separately timed finish choice that is cured before the appointment ends. Regular polish is the finish included with each listed base pedicure and continues drying afterward. Ask the salon how either option fits your footwear, timing, existing product, and future removal plan.

The active booking contract specifies the finish names, prices, and reserved time. It does not specify wear duration, chip resistance, natural-nail effects, or a removal technique.

No salon should promise an exact number of chip-free days. Toenail growth, footwear, pool exposure, impact, preparation, and aftercare all affect wear. Compare the maintenance path rather than treating a duration estimate as a guarantee.

The base pedicure still controls the experience

Element Nail Bar lists eight base pedicures: Classic, Deluxe, Organic Spa, Pearl Spa, Róse Berry, Jelly Spa, CBD Experience, and Gold Enchantment. The active booking catalog confirms each exact name, price, and total duration. Regular polish is included with each base pedicure; optional add-ons are booked separately.

Gel Polish is a separate $15, 15-minute pedicure add-on. Adding it changes the selected finish and the reserved time, but the catalog does not say that it changes the unlisted steps of the chosen base service. A Classic booking with Gel Polish and an Organic Spa booking with regular polish remain different base reservations.

Use the pedicure service overview to compare the eight base listings. Then check the menu’s current add-ons for Gel Polish, French, Callus Removal, or other available additions. This order produces a clearer reservation than searching for a single package called “gel pedicure.”

Removal deserves a place in the original booking

If product is already on your toenails, describe it when you book. The active service-facts contract does not specify an included removal method or removal procedure for the Gel Polish add-on, so this guide does not assign one. The salon can identify the correct reservation after you explain what is currently present.

Mention gel, regular polish, glitter, art, or a toenail enhancement rather than trying to remove or classify it for the booking form. That gives the salon the information needed to confirm whether another service or more time should be reserved.

Phoenix footwear and pool routines

Phoenix weather puts sandals into rotation for much of the year, which makes both the color and the surrounding skin more visible. Regular polish pairs well with open-toe shoes after the appointment because there is less pressure on the fresh finish. Gel offers the advantage of leaving with cured color when sandals are not practical.

The active booking contract does not specify how swimming, footwear, or travel affects either finish. If those plans matter to your choice, ask the salon what it can confirm about the available finishes.

Travel outside Phoenix adds another timing question: will you want professional removal before the next color? If you choose gel immediately before a long trip, know where that later service will happen. If you choose regular polish, bring the shade or a compatible color if small touch-ups matter.

A five-point choice

Use these questions to reach a decision without overthinking it:

  1. Do I need to put on closed shoes soon after the appointment?
  2. Am I likely to want a different color within a short period?
  3. Can I return for professional gel removal?
  4. Is the separately booked $15 Gel Polish finish the option I want?
  5. What pedicure tier do I want before polish is considered?

If the answers favor a lamp-cured finish, choose Gel Polish. If the included finish and continued drying fit your plan, choose regular polish. Ask the salon about wear and removal rather than assuming a guaranteed result.

Reserve the finish and the service together

Element Nail Bar is at 6022 N 16th St in Phoenix. Before booking, write down the existing finish, the pedicure tier you want, and any removal or art. A useful note might read: “Classic Pedicure, remove existing gel, new gel color, no design.” Another could say: “Organic Spa, regular polish, bringing open-toe shoes.”

Reserve your Element 16 pedicure only after the complete scope is selected. If you are uncertain about the current product or the right removal category, call 602-607-5686. The front desk can clarify the reservation; the technician can confirm the cosmetic plan after seeing the nails.
